extracted.intended_audience: high school English teachers, curriculum developers, and assessors (grades 11–12)
extracted.subtask_description: Common Core–aligned standards and a companion 4-point rubric for writing narratives (grades 11–12) that develop real or imagined experiences/events using effective technique, details, and coherent event sequences. Intended to guide instruction, assessment, and student expectations for advanced secondary narrative writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: W.11-12.3 — Narrative Writing (Overarching Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching expectation for grade 11–12 narrative writing: develop events/experiences with deliberate technique, specific/detail-rich language, and coherent sequencing that produces a clear effect or outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: W.11-12.3.A — Engagement & Orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on immediately situating the reader: present the central situation/problem and its significance, clarify perspective(s) (narrator/POV), introduce characters as needed, and ensure the narrative begins with a coherent orientation that leads into the events.

rubrics_metrics.name: W.11-12.3.B — Narrative Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ a variety of techniques (e.g., realistic dialogue, controlled pacing, evocative description, reflective commentary, interweaving plotlines) to deepen characterization and advance the narrative; choose techniques purposefully to develop the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: W.11-12.3.C — Sequencing & Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence events deliberately (flashback/foreshadowing, chronologic or nonchronologic ordering, parallel plots) so each event contributes to an overall coherence and the intended tone/outcome; sequencing should create cumulative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: W.11-12.3.D — Language & Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize accurate, specific diction, concrete telling details, and sensory imagery to create vividness; vary syntax and sentence-level craft to enhance voice and imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: W.11-12.3.E — Conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude by deriving or implying meaning from the narrative events—closure, reflection, or insight should feel earned by what precedes it and underscore the narrative's significance or outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companion Rubric — Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Engages reader; establishes context, POV, narrator, characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a scored category on a 4-point scale (4 Exemplary → 1 Beginning). Evaluates how effectively the opening engages and orients the reader, sets context, establishes point(s) of view and introduces narrator/characters in service of the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companion Rubric — Narrative Techniques
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored on a 4-point scale; assesses the purposeful use and effectiveness of dialogue, pacing, descriptive detail, reflection, and other narrative devices to develop events and characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companion Rubric — Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Smooth event progression toward intended tone/outcome
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored category that measures coherence of event sequencing and how well events build toward the story's intended tone or outcome (e.g., suspense, resolution, growth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Companion Rubric — Style/Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Precise word choice, sensory detail, varied syntax
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates diction, imagery, sentence variety, and command of standard conventions; scored on the same 4-point scale for degree of control and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companion Rubric — Conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Follows from and reflects on the narrative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the ending logically arises from the story and provides meaningful reflection or resolution; included as a scored category (4 → 1).
